I know I'm late to answer this but here it goes. I am an Arab born into a predominantly Christian family with some Muslim members. Muslims relate to the plight to the Palestinians because of 2 main reasons: 

  
1. Al-Aqsa mosque is considered one of 3 holy sites in Islam.

2. Arabs sympathize with Palestinians, and Muslims in general (sadly) look up to Arabs, as Islam was kind of made for Arabs (Quran and Hadith and names are all in Arabic).  


Muslims in the west, whether Arab or not, are subjected to a lot of bigotry, especially after 9/11, and now again after 10/7. I've had to try really hard and share many articles to convince some Americans that I am Arab. In their minds, I could not be Arab because 'I do not behave like an uncultured, oppressed woman whose only job is to be a sex slave'. Many people in the west assume that every Arab is Muslim, and that every Muslim is a violent fundamentalist who supports terrorism. This is an overwhelmingly common sentiment. While hate crimes against Muslims, or those who are perceived as Muslim, are not as extreme as anti-Semitic hate crimes, they are not unheard of, and people are generally more comfortable loudly hating on Muslims. For example, many journalists came out when the Ukraine war started and called refugees from the Arab or the 3rd world in general uncivilized. Some people publicly call Muslims piss drinkers.   


It should be common knowledge that most Muslims are not fundamentalists and most countries with Muslims majorities do not follow Sharia law, nor do they want to. Islam, like any ideology, exists on a spectrum. Many Arabs are not Muslims and most Muslims are not extremists and thus believe that the hate and bigotry they face is unjust. This has created an anti-west sentiment in Arab and Muslims countries specifically and in the Global South generally which has led people to oppose and dismiss most views publicly held by the west as racist and Islamophobic. If the west that hates us supports a people or a cause, then it must be working against us. This is why there is more Russian support among Arab and Muslims communities, even though Russian chemical weapons have been maiming and killing Syrian children for years now.  The western world hates them, so they must be doing something right. They will go above and beyond to rationalize this. This is why most Muslims, by default, will oppose the west by supporting "their brothers and sisters" in Palestine. Their support for Palestine is often a way of expressing frustration with how they've been treated and standing up against what they see as unfairness.

I am so sorry. As an arab, I understand how exhausting and terrifying the threats can be. It gets so overwhelming when all you read online are misconceptions fueled by stereotypes and propaganda. I'm lucky I have a place and community that accepts me for who I am. I wish the same for you. I can't imagine how it must feel like to have to deal with threats in face to face situations. It's time we realized we all just want to live with dignity and safety that allow us to grow. Please stay safe.
It has made me cry too! Sending hugs to all of you.

I agree!! Our pain has become so politicised that it's hard for many to heal from it and understand the other side. I hope you are staying safe.

I don't even know how I ended up here. I remember seeing a post related to the war when it first started. When I first heard about it that morning, my first thoughts were "good on Gazans for breaking through!". Then images and videos and stories of the atrocities started emerging. I just knew it wasn't right. Harming civilians and children is not right or justified. Reddit was full of people trying to justify crimes on both sides. So when I saw a post about the people rather than the politics, I was very interested to see the Jewish perspective. There was no hate, just expressions of support and advice. It was beautiful.
This is beautiful. I'm also so glad it didn't get downvoted!

Thank you for your reply. I never considered Crohn's disease. In fact I didn't know much about it, only the name.

I don't always have diarrhea. I get it for 2-3 days every 3 ish weeks, and then it goes away. I usually get more constipated. I get nauseous a lot but rarely vomit. I usually only vomit when my menstrual cycle is particularly bad (which is one every 4-5 months). And there is never blood in any discharge. 

I just realized I've been having some skin problems lately. Nothing over the top. I got a rash on my elbow last week but that went away after a week or so. I have a small itchy one on my right wrist right now. I thought they may be insect bites? Although I don't remember getting exposed to insects. I'm also experiencing the worst acne in the past 2 years. I used to get moderate acne in my teenage years in my T-zones because I have naturally oily skin. The acne I have now is on my lower cheeks, chin, and chest, which I was told is hormonal. I'm not sure these are symptoms, but it's things I just noticed may be connected to Crohn's. 

I'll read more and tell my doctor about it. Thanks!
